proxy_language: Proto-Indo-European (late/Northwest-adjacent dialect stage) used as a deliberately weak stand-in; nothing is known of Ahrensburgian speech
proxy_rationale: The Ahrensburgian (c. 12,900-11,700 BP, Younger Dryas reindeer hunters of the N European Plain and S Scandinavia) is known only from lithics (tanged Havelte/Ahrensburg points), reindeer-hunting sites (Stellmoor) and Meiendorf-type camps. No language is recoverable, and the later languages of the region (Germanic, Baltic, Uralic, Saami, pre-IE substrates) cannot be projected back 13,000 years. As a game convention, a reconstructed root-based language with well-documented morphology is the most defensible tool; PIE is used with explicit acknowledgment that the link is purely conventional and that a pre-Indo-European/unknown language is far more likely in reality. Names are built from reconstructed roots (asterisked) in scholarly PIE notation with simplified laryngeal-free transliteration.
phonology: Reconstructed PIE (Fortson/Beekes style): stops *p *t *k *k' (palatovelar, written ḱ) *kʷ; voiced *b *d *g *ǵ *gʷ (rare *b); aspirated *bʰ *dʰ *gʰ *ǵʰ *gʷʰ; fricative *s; sonorants *m *n *l *r *y(j) *w; laryngeals *h1 *h2 *h3 (omitted or written h1/h2/h3 sparingly); vowels *e *o *a (rare) *i *u with length (ē ō ā). Stress was pitch-accented and mobile, but is not written.
phonotactics: Syllable structure (C)(C)V(C)(C) with sonorant/obstruent nucleus alternations (*i/y, *u/w, *r̥ *l̥ *m̥ *n̥ as syllabic). Roots are typically CeC, with e as the basic vowel and o/zero grade in derivatives. Onset clusters mostly s+stop, stop+liquid/glide; no *b-heavy or voiced-aspirate+voiced-aspirate roots (Bartholomae/Grassmann-type root constraints: no two plain voiced stops, no *d...g clusters). Nominative -s, no word-final voiced obstruents in practice. Words rarely begin with a vowel except laryngeal-initial roots.
orthography: Scholarly PIE reconstruction notation in Latin script, simplified for the game: ḱ ǵ ǵʰ for palatovelars, kʷ gʷ gʰ bʰ dʰ for labiovelar/aspirates, vowels e o a i u with macrons (ē ō ā) optional, syllabic sonorants written with ringed or plain vowel+sonorant (r̥ as 'r' with ring or as 'ṛ'); asterisk dropped in names. In plain-ASCII fallback use k' for ḱ, g' for ǵ, kw, gw, gh, bh, dh.
morphology: Root + thematic vowel (-e/-o-) or athematic suffixes; ablaut e/o/zero grade. Nouns: nominative -s, accusative -m, genitive -(o)s/-es/-os or -syo (thematic), locative -i, ablative -(o)s/-ed (thematic), instrumental -(e)h1, plural -es/-os, neuter -m/-Ø. Derivation: agent -tor/-ter (*-ter), instrument -tro-/-dʰlo-, abstract -ti-, adjectives -(i)ó-, -ent-/-nt- participles, patronymic/possessive -yo-. No reduplication needed except perfective/intensive roots (e.g. *de-dʰeh1-).
compounding: Head-final determinative (tatpurusha) and possessive (bahuvrihi) compounds with compositional -o- linking vowel: first member as stem (often -o- stem) + head. 'X of Y' is either a genitive phrase (Y-genitive X) or a compound Y-o-X. Agent names as root+*-tor/-ter or *-o- compounds ('X-maker' = X-o-dʰh1-o-/ *dʰeh1- root as second member). Bahuvrihi names like 'swift-footed' = adj. stem + noun stem + suffix.
noun_phrase_order: Adjective before noun and agreeing in case/number/gender; genitive before head noun (Y-genitive X) in the compound/phrasal default; demonstratives precede; relative constructions not needed for names. Compounds are strictly modifier-head.

worked_examples.name: Gwhenotor
worked_examples.gloss: *gʷʰen- 'strike/kill' + agent *-tor (reindeer implied by context; no PIE reindeer root is secure)

sources: Fortson, Indo-European Language and Culture, 2nd ed., 2010
Mallory & Adams, Encyclopedia of Indo-European Culture, 1997
Glottolog and ASJP (for confirming no attested linguistic link)
notes: No word may be identical to a Modern Irish, Scottish Gaelic or Manx word. Linguistically the Ahrensburgian is unknowable; PIE is a convention only and may not be presented as the language they spoke. The current game strings (Xubayir, Wudik, Nuxadud, etc.) violate PIE phonotactics (x, initial kw/ux clusters and invented CV-syllable fillers) and should be replaced by root-based forms.
